notes.sol: Reference SEs are from the source’s NoChanges tables, not the later reweighting, recoding, unit-of-analysis or topic-model extensions. Original Table A5, p. 7, was opened separately from the human report.
notes.claude: Reconciled with the second labeller (see reconciliation.md). The final judgement is the structured label; notes_blind_original keeps the pre-reconciliation blind notes, which are historical and superseded wherever they conflict with the final label.
notes.claude_blind_original_historical: Severity P1 for C1-C3 is a judgement: Table A5/Figure 1 is the paper's main observational figure, and the larger SEs make the key non-violent CIs overlap (the report's 'one exception' to reproducibility). P2 is defensible because the main interaction model (Table A3) 'replicate[s] perfectly'. The report's description is mixed: separately, the shipped replicate_fig_1.R also gives larger CIs, which do not overlap because it omits two controls (PASTNV, PASTV) present in the A5 code. So no shipped script regenerates the printed SEs. The A5 SEs come from ggeffects::ggpredict, which is deterministic but may vary by version; the report does not establish the cause. A reconciler could therefore argue 'not_checkable' for C1-C3. I did not choose that, because the report tested the unchanged code and found materially different values. Side observation: replicate_table_A5.R assigns Status labels using `preds$x==0` (an object not defined in that script) instead of `preds_status$x`, which could mislabel the status rows if run standalone. Row labels in the report ('Majority/dominant', 'Minority/disadvantaged') map to the SI's 'Not excluded'/'Excluded'.
